entries.name: Sexually transmitted infections
entries.content:
Sexually transmitted infections (STIs) are diseases that are primarily spread through sexual contact. Here are some common STIs, their causes, transmission methods, symptoms, and effects:

Chlamydia: Chlamydia is caused by bacteria and is one of the most common STIs. It can be transmitted through vaginal, anal, or oral sex. Many people with chlamydia do not experience symptoms, but when symptoms occur, they can include abnormal genital discharge and burning during urination. If left untreated, chlamydia can cause serious reproductive problems, including infertility.

Gonorrhea: Gonorrhea is another bacterial infection that spreads through sexual contact. It often infects the genital tract, but it can also affect the rectum, throat, and eyes. Symptoms may include a burning sensation when urinating, discharge from the genitals, and, in women, pelvic pain. Untreated gonorrhea can lead to pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) in women and can cause infertility in both men and women.

Syphilis: Syphilis is a bacterial infection that progresses in stages. The first stage typically presents as a painless sore at the infection site. If untreated, the disease progresses to a rash, often on the hands and feet, and eventually to severe damage to organs such as the heart and brain. Syphilis is spread through direct contact with a syphilis sore during vaginal, anal, or oral sex.

Human papillomavirusz: HPV is a viral infection that can cause genital warts and is also associated with certain cancers, including cervical cancer. HPV is transmitted through skin-to-skin contact during sexual activity. Many people with HPV do not develop symptoms, but those who do might notice warts on the genital or anal areas. Vaccination can prevent the most harmful strains of HPV.

Herpes simplex virus: HSV causes genital herpes, which is characterized by painful sores or blisters on the genital or anal area. HSV is spread through vaginal, anal, or oral sex, even when sores are not present. The virus can remain dormant in the body and reactivate, causing recurrent outbreaks. There is no cure for herpes, but antiviral medications can manage symptoms.

HIV: HIV or human immunodeficiency virus, attacks the body's immune system and can lead to AIDS (acquired immunodeficiency syndrome) if untreated. HIV is transmitted through contact with infected bodily fluids, such as blood, semen, vaginal fluids, and breast milk. Early symptoms can resemble the flu, but the virus can remain asymptomatic for years. HIV weakens the immune system, making it difficult to fight off infections and diseases. Antiretroviral therapy can control the virus and prevent the progression to AIDS.

Trichomoniasis: Trichomoniasis is a parasitic infection caused by Trichomonas vaginalis. It is spread through vaginal sex. Many people do not have symptoms, but when they do occur, they can include itching, burning, redness, or soreness of the genitals and discomfort during urination or sex. In women, there may be a thin discharge with an unusual smell. Trichomoniasis can increase the risk of other STIs.

These STIs can have significant health impacts if left untreated, including chronic pain, infertility, complications during pregnancy, and increased risk of contracting other infections. Prevention methods include practicing safe sex, such as using condoms, and getting regular STI screenings. Vaccinations are available for certain STIs like HPV.

entries.name: Breast size
entries.content:
Asian women generally have smaller breast sizes compared to women from other regions. This includes women from China, Taiwan, Southeast Asia, Japan, Korea, Mongolia, and India. In these areas, the average breast size is typically between A and B cups. Sizes above D are considered uncommon, and E cups and larger are rare. Additionally, the way bra sizes are measured in Japan differs from Western countries, making Japanese cup sizes effectively smaller.

In contrast, women of European and Caucasian descent, including those from Europe, the United States, and possibly South America, tend to have larger breasts. The average breast size in these regions can reach up to D cups. However, larger breast sizes above D are less rare compared to Asia.

entries.name: Semen
entries.content: Semen is typically white, while extremely thick semen can appear light yellow. Light yellow semen usually forms if a man refrains from ejaculation for about a month. Frequent masturbation or ejaculation can decrease the concentration of semen, making it more transparent and increasing the odor of the semen on the penis. Semen generally has a very bitter taste, but consuming foods high in sugar, such as pineapple, can make it taste sweeter.

entries.name: Appearance
entries.content: Asians often appear younger than Westerners, even into adulthood, especially women from East Asian countries like China, Japan, Korea, and Taiwan. Westerners generally look older than Asians, regardless of their actual age. By East Asian standards, Westerners can look at least ten to twenty years older than Asians, even when they are the same age.
